alejandra: FYI saw a weird packing churn in ap-se1 this morning - lots of tiny GPU pods getting preempted and rebound across AZs.
chao: Yep, traced to network attach latency on ap-se1c. Scheduler flagged nodes degraded and routed to ap-se1a/b, which then hit affinity conflicts.
alejandra: snippet: ```[2026-03-22T09:10:01Z] attach_latency=420ms node=ap-se1c 
[2026-03-22T09:10:02Z] scheduler_mark=node=ap-se1c state=transient_unavailable reason=attach_latency 
[2026-03-22T09:10:03Z] route_to=ap-se1b pod=tiny-gpu-worker fallback=true 
[2026-03-22T09:10:05Z] eviction=pod=tiny-gpu-worker node=ap-se1b reason=affinity_conflict```
infra-bot: Alert: conntrack-pressure-ap-se1c detected (60% nodes reporting >80% table usage). AZ-fallback policy triggered.
sre-oncall: Putting a mitigations list here: 1) temporary scheduler threshold bump for ap-se1 (150ms->500ms) canary 5% 2) daemonset to increase conntrack_max on affected nodes 3) short-term reserved lane (2 GPUs) per AZ for tiny ephemeral pods to avoid cross-AZ shuffle.
chao: I can open the scheduler PR for the canary. @sre-oncall can you handle the sysctl roll?
sre-oncall: Will roll conntrack bump to 25% first, monitoring for regressions.
alejandra: I'll add alerting for fallback-rate and eviction-rate per AZ. Postmortem pending after stabilization. :thumbsup:
